question.worked_solution:
Since parallel lines have equal slopes, both lines should have the same slope.

First, let's find the slope of the line passing through the points $(2,1)$ and $(3,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{-1-1}{3-2} \\  & =-\frac{2}{1} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we wish to find a line that has a slope of $-2$ and passes through the point $(0,2).$ To find the equation of this line, we use the point-slope form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-2 & =-2(x-0) \\ y-2 & =-2x \\ y & =-2x+2\end{aligned}
$$
